title: Solana's emergency unwind is unspecified while Ethereum's is complete, and its consolidation step cites the mainnet controller
content:
The Solana Emergency Protocol is asymmetric with its Ethereum counterpart. Where Ethereum specifies redeem-all, swap-all and burn-all as concrete calls, A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.3.3 declares the goal — "recover the liquidity from Solana Protocols and centralize it in the Keel ALM Controller" — and then both children, Integrations (…3.3.1) and Reserves (…3.3.2), say only "this will be specified in a future iteration of the Keel Artifact."

The next step is stranger. A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.3.4, the Solana AtomicSwap recovery action for consolidating into USDS, gives the code as `mainnetController.swapUSDCToUSDS(usdc.balanceOf(address(proxy))` and links to the Ethereum swap documentation. That is an Ethereum call with an Ethereum contract handle sitting inside the Solana emergency section — either a copy-paste from the mainnet playbook, or shorthand for a step that only happens after the following one.

That following step, A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.2.3.5, is "Bridge to Ethereum Mainnet": returning recovered liquidity to Keel's Ethereum ALM Controller. So the intended sequence is plausibly recover on Solana, bridge home, then consolidate — in which case the swap step is out of order as written.

Either way the practical exposure is real and compounds an earlier constraint: Solana positions must come home to be wound down, the bridge back is rate-limited at 25M with a 10M/day slope, and the two clauses that would tell an operator how to exit Solana venues are blank. The frontier chain has the weakest keys, the smallest limits, and the least specified escape route.
description: Redeem All Positions defers both Integrations and Reserves to a future iteration, and the AtomicSwap recovery action is written as mainnetController.swapUSDCToUSDS on the ALM Proxy balance.
